questions.question_text: How many total CE hours must a Washington broker complete for the first license renewal?
questions.explanation: WAC 308-124A-785 requires 90 clock hours for the first active renewal, all started after the date first licensed: a 30-hour Real Estate Law course, a 30-hour Advanced Practices course, and 30 hours of approved continuing education that must include the 3-hour core curriculum and the Washington real estate fair housing requirement.

questions.question_text: How many clock hours of Washington real estate fair housing education must a broker who completed fair housing in prelicense education include at renewal?
distractors: None — it is a one-time prelicense requirement
questions.explanation: RCW 18.85.211(2) requires three of the 30 renewal hours to be Washington real estate fair housing education. The six-hour version applies only to a licensee who did not complete fair housing education during initial qualification for licensure (WAC 308-124A-790(1)(c)) — and since June 1, 2022 the prelicense Fundamentals course has included three hours of fair housing and consumer protection (RCW 18.85.101(1)(c)), so a broker licensed since then takes 3 hours, not 6.

questions.question_text: A newly licensed broker asks what the '3-hour WA Core' course covers during first renewal. What is its focus?
questions.explanation: The 3-hour WA Core course (also called Current Issues) covers contemporary issues in Washington real estate practice. Under WAC 308-124A-800 it is recommended by the real estate commission, approved by the director, and must be completed within 24 months of the licensee's renewal date; hours started 24 to 36 months out count as ordinary CE but not as core.

questions.question_text: A broker completed 60 of the 90 first-renewal CE hours. Which required course is most likely missing from her transcript?
questions.explanation: The first renewal requires a 30-hour Advanced Practices course, a 30-hour Real Estate Law course, and 30 hours of CE that must include the 3-hour WA Core and the fair housing requirement (WAC 308-124A-785). A broker sitting at 60 hours has most likely finished Advanced Practices and the 30-hour CE block and still owes the 30-hour Real Estate Law course.

questions.question_text: When do first-renewal CE hours begin accruing for a Washington broker?
questions.explanation: First-renewal CE hours start accruing after a broker receives their initial license. Pre-license education hours do not count toward the 90-hour first-renewal CE requirement.

questions.question_text: How many CE hours are required for each subsequent license renewal after the first?
questions.explanation: After the initial 90-hour first renewal, each subsequent renewal requires 30 hours of continuing education: 3-hour WA Core, 3-hour Fair Housing, and 24 hours of electives.

questions.question_text: How many hours of Fair Housing CE are required at each subsequent renewal?
questions.explanation: RCW 18.85.211(2) requires three of the 30 renewal hours to be Washington real estate fair housing education at every active renewal. The six-hour version is required only of a licensee whose initial qualification for licensure did not include fair housing education (WAC 308-124A-790(1)(c)).

questions.question_text: A broker completes 25 CE hours in each year of her 2-year renewal cycle, or 50 hours total. How many of the excess hours may she carry forward?
questions.explanation: WAC 308-124A-790(1)(b) allows up to 15 clock hours beyond the 30 submitted for a renewal to be carried forward to the following renewal date. This broker has 20 excess hours, so 15 carry forward and the remaining 5 are lost.

questions.question_text: How often must a Washington broker renew their license?
questions.explanation: Washington uses a biennial (every 2 years) renewal cycle. At least 15 of the required 30 CE hours must be completed within the 24 months immediately preceding renewal.

questions.question_text: A broker completed all 30 CE hours 30 months before her renewal date. Does this satisfy Washington's CE timing rules?
questions.correct_answer: No, 15 hours must fall within 24 months
distractors: Yes, the hours are within 48 months
No, hours older than 12 months never count
questions.explanation: WAC 308-124A-790(1) lets renewal hours be started within 48 months of the renewal date, so hours earned 30 months out are not wasted. But subsection (1)(a) requires a minimum of 15 clock hours within 24 months of the renewal date, and the 3-hour core and the fair housing hours must fall inside that 24-month window. Completing everything 30 months out fails those requirements.

questions.question_text: A broker's license expired 60 days ago. What is the late renewal penalty?
questions.explanation: WAC 308-124A-775 sets the broker renewal fee at $233 and late renewal with penalty at $273 — a $40 penalty on top of the renewal fee. A late application does not cancel the license; under RCW 18.85.191 cancellation happens only if the renewal fee is not received within one year of expiration.

questions.question_text: Within what period after expiration is late renewal still available before a Washington broker's license is canceled?
questions.explanation: RCW 18.85.191 provides that a late renewal application requires a penalty fee, and that "the license of a person whose license renewal fee is not received within one year from the date of expiration is canceled." Washington has no 120-day grace period. Once the license is canceled, the licensee must reinstate under WAC 308-124A-780.

questions.question_text: A broker's license expired 150 days ago. What must she pay to restore her license?
questions.explanation: At 150 days past expiration the license is late but not canceled — cancellation happens only after one year (RCW 18.85.191). The broker pays the $273 late renewal fee for brokers under WAC 308-124A-775, which is the $233 renewal fee plus the $40 penalty. The $100 reinstatement penalty fine applies only after cancellation.

questions.question_text: A broker is transferring from one firm to another. What step must be completed?
questions.correct_answer: Notify the DOL of the transfer
questions.explanation: When a broker transfers between firms, the DOL must be notified. The broker keeps the same license and license number but must be affiliated with a firm to actively practice real estate.

questions.question_text: A broker left her firm last month and has not yet joined another. Can she continue practicing real estate?
questions.correct_answer: No, must be with a firm to practice
questions.explanation: Washington requires brokers to be affiliated with a firm to actively practice real estate. A broker who is between firms cannot conduct real estate business until they affiliate with a new firm and notify the DOL.
